q: H₀ in a test of whether a policy works is usually …
why: The null is the 'nothing going on' claim.

q: x̄ = 103, μ₀ = 100, s = 15, n = 100. Test statistic z?
Not rejecting H₀ proves there is no effect.
why: Myth. The sample may have been too small to see it.

q: A statistically significant effect can be economically tiny.
why: Fact: with huge samples tiny effects become significant.
